whatsHappening.background: Ukraine’s current crisis escalated in 2014 when Russia annexed Crimea and fighting began in eastern Ukraine. In February 2022, Russia launched a full-scale invasion, turning the conflict into Europe’s largest war in decades. The war continues to cause displacement, civilian deaths and injuries, attacks on infrastructure, and long-term humanitarian needs.

civilianImpact.experiences: Civilians have endured displacement, bereavement, trauma, damaged homes, interrupted schooling, power outages, and pressure on health systems. Repeated strikes on energy and water infrastructure make daily life harder, especially for children, older adults, and people near front-line areas.

howToHelp.summary: Ukraine’s humanitarian crisis remains urgent because millions still need shelter, protection, health care, winter support, and help rebuilding their lives.

learnMore.text: The crisis grew from the 2014 conflict into a full-scale war and a continuing humanitarian emergency.

whatsHappening.background: The war affects civilians through displacement, injury, psychological trauma, damaged infrastructure, economic hardship, and disrupted public services. Needs are highest near front-line areas and in communities repeatedly hit by aerial attacks.

civilianImpact.experiences: For many Ukrainians, the crisis means living far from home, rebuilding after attacks, and trying to maintain daily life under uncertainty. Recovery is made harder by damaged housing, energy outages, explosive remnants, and the ongoing risk of new strikes.

image.alt: War damage in Kyiv after an attack

howToHelp.summary: Even beyond active fighting, families need shelter support, psychosocial care, winter assistance, education support, and reconstruction help.

learnMore.text: The civilian toll includes displacement, trauma, damaged infrastructure, and long-term rebuilding challenges.

whatsHappening.background: Support is most effective when it goes to organizations already assisting civilians with shelter, food, medical care, winter support, child protection, and recovery. Public attention also matters because long wars can fade from view even while civilian needs remain high.
